1537990785781510151.a: I'm no expert but my major is in a field which includes RADAR and I used to repair/calibrate them part time during college. LIDAR is cool if you are going 2 MPH. Not so cool if you are going 70 MPH. 70MPH seems simple until you learn the inverse square law in physics.

1537990787765481475.a: The decommissioned military RADARs I worked on for example were 90 degree sweeps at 1 million watts instantaneous or 1 kW average. You could see 300 miles or so. To see just 150 miles you need only 250kW/250W. To see 75 miles 62.5kW/62.5W. See the issue here?

1537990789485146113.a: Now, the issue is that LIDAR uses infrared lasers. We use infrared to cook meat.

1537991996823859201.a: Now could you underpower the LIDAR system and use fancy algorithms to compensate for the lack of power? Of course. If you don't care about having reliable data or a working system at all. My point is, unless someone shows me physics equations, LIDAR is an expensive scam on cars.

1537992962818224130.a:
If you are lost on my point I will be explicit:
The faster you go the longer it takes to stop. You need the LIDAR to reliably see at least 2 or 3 times farther than your stopping distance or you will crash anyway despite the collision warning. The car can't stop dead and you live

1537994128134270976.a: Now, now, now, lets get back to RADAR. What do most cars including most Teslas use instead of LIDAR for collision avoidance? RADAR. Which can see to the horizon with almost no power output. Air/Dust absorbs infrared so radio waves are the obvious choice.

1537994934422122496.a: Tesla temporarily has stopped installing RADARs because, like LIDAR, current market RADAR technology is garbage. RADAR as a technique is fine but Tesla needs high resolution video RADAR which probably only exists in the military space. If only Tesla knew a military contractor.

1537994936011743232.a: Conveniently, Tesla just patented such a device. With RF video you can do sensor fusion. You cannot do sensor fusion with current market car RADARS because they are about the quality of a fisher price toy in the 80s.

1538286166843203584.a:
For Vintage Shortwave Radio enthusiasts, I just uploaded a service manual for the Sangean ATS-818 and Radio Shack DX-390. 1992 Vintage. Doh, I made myself feel old.
I needed to figure out how to defeat the battery alarm to upgrade to Lithium Ion batteries.
archive.org/details/sangea…

1538286168365797382.a: Answer: You kinda can't. The radio is based on a clock radio. Yeah, like the kind you use to wake up with. So it needs a dry cell type memory battery or an alkaline will work. The chip, in the die, requires a specific voltage differential between primary and secondary battery.

1538286169741484032.a: Solution: Suck it up and spend another $1 on a second boost converter. Alternately, torture yourself by installing a non-stupid memory battery like a CR-2032. Radio Shack sold batteries and Sangean radios were likely going to be used in places that didn't have weird batteries. 🤷‍♂️

1538286968139919361.a: The memory battery is important if you use this like you would have used it in 1992. Probably as a clock radio. Probably on a seagoing vessel. The memory battery is far more important on the DX-392/ATS-818ACS where you can schedule a recording on the builtin cassette recorder.
